identity.name: Shellac
identity.chemical_class: Natural low-molecular-weight polyester resin (mixture of mono- and polyesters of hydroxyaliphatic and sesquiterpenoid acids)

function.mechanism: Applied as a thin external coating; after solvent evaporation it forms a protective glossy film and can further self-esterify/polymerize.

adi.basis: EFSA 2024 derived ADI from NOAEL 400 mg/kg bw/day (UF 100) for wax-free shellac produced by physical decolouring; temporary for chemically bleached wax-free shellac pending impurity data.

efsa.key_finding: P95 exposure exceedances were observed in several age groups, but EFSA concluded low exceedance under conservative assumptions did not indicate a safety concern.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database entry for SHELLAC, BLEACHED (INS 904) reports ADI as NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: For chemically bleached shellac, EFSA identified unresolved organochlorine impurity characterization and recommended specification tightening (including chloroform/lead controls).
Human dermatology evidence indicates contact allergy potential (e.g., 3.77% positivity among patch-tested suspected dermatitis cases), mainly relevant to dermal/cosmetic/occupational exposure.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported no genotoxicity concern for shellac materials evaluated.
EFSA subchronic and chronic studies did not indicate major systemic toxicity at tested dose ranges used for ADI derivation.
JECFA comment: present external coating/glazing uses were not of toxicological concern.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2024 reported 95th percentile exceedances in non-brand-loyal and maximum-level scenarios, but concluded low exceedance under conservative assumptions did not indicate a safety concern.

risk_assessment.rationale: Shellac remains authorized with generally reassuring toxicology, but EFSA's temporary ADI status for chemically bleached material, unresolved organochlorine impurity identity/levels, and high-percentile ADI exceedances in some groups justify a moderate tier rather than limited/risk_free.
key_factors: EFSA 2024 ADI = 4 mg/kg bw/day with temporary caveat for chemically bleached wax-free shellac
P95 ADI exceedance in several age groups under conservative exposure scenarios
No IARC listing for shellac and no major jurisdictional ban identified
JECFA ADI not specified with historical conclusion of no toxicological concern at present uses
